facts.text: OpenUSD, OpenDRIVE, OpenCRG, OpenSCENARIO, OpenLABEL, OpenODD and OpenXOntology are agreed file formats for exchanging descriptions of worlds, roads, road surfaces, event sequences, labels, operating domains or shared vocabularies between simulation tools.
facts.quote: These are agreed file formats that let different simulation tools exchange the same description of a world, a road, a road surface, a sequence of events, a set of labels, an operating domain or a shared vocabulary.

facts.text: Most of the scene description formats discussed are published by ASAM (Association for Standardization of Automation and Measuring Systems), a German-based industry association, and collectively called the OpenX family.
facts.quote: Most of these formats are published by ASAM (Association for Standardization of Automation and Measuring Systems), a German-based industry association, and are collectively called the OpenX family.

facts.text: OpenUSD (Universal Scene Description) is an open format originating in the film industry and now widely used in simulation for complete three-dimensional scenes and assets, including geometry, materials and hierarchy.
facts.quote: OpenUSD (Universal Scene Description) is an open format from the film industry, now widely used in simulation, for complete three-dimensional scenes and assets: geometry, materials, hierarchy.

facts.text: OpenUSD is domain-neutral and can represent a mine as well as a city.
facts.quote: It is domain-neutral, so a mine fits as well as a city.

facts.text: The booklet considers OpenUSD at least as strategically important as OpenDRIVE for the heavy off-road collision-mitigation validation program.
facts.quote: The booklet calls it "at least as strategically important as OpenDRIVE" for this program [Chapter 11].

facts.text: OpenDRIVE version 1.9.0, dated May 2026, describes road networks including lanes, lane geometry, road marks and junctions.
facts.quote: OpenDRIVE (version 1.9.0, May 2026) describes road networks: lanes, lane geometry, road marks, junctions.

facts.text: OpenDRIVE assumes roads and can model haul roads, but dig faces, stockpiles and free terrain require additional representations.
facts.quote: It assumes roads. Haul roads can be modeled; dig faces, stockpiles and free terrain cannot without additional representations [Chapter 9].

facts.text: OpenCRG describes fine road-surface height profiles and is useful for haul-road roughness, but not for open terrain.
facts.quote: OpenCRG describes the fine height profile of a road surface, useful for haul-road roughness but not for open terrain [Chapter 9].

facts.text: OpenSCENARIO describes actor movement over time; its XML text format, version 1.4.0 dated 2026, supports precise synchronized maneuvers.
facts.quote: OpenSCENARIO describes what happens over time: which actors move where and when. Two forms exist: an XML text format (version 1.4.0, 2026) for precise synchronized maneuvers

facts.text: OpenSCENARIO's domain-specific language version 2.2.0, dated March 2026, treats abstract scenarios, parameter ranges and performance indicators as first-class concepts.
facts.quote: a domain-specific language, DSL (version 2.2.0, March 2026), in which abstract scenarios, parameter ranges and performance indicators are first-class concepts.

facts.text: Both the XML and DSL forms of OpenSCENARIO carry a road-traffic domain model.
facts.quote: Both carry a road-traffic domain model [Chapter 9].

facts.text: OpenLABEL defines annotation of recorded data, specifying which object is where in each frame; the booklet considers OpenLABEL useful for dataset labeling but did not verify it.
facts.quote: OpenLABEL defines how to annotate recorded data (which object is where in which frame); the booklet notes it as useful for dataset labeling but did not verify it [Chapter 9].

facts.text: OpenODD version 1.0.0, dated 3 April 2025, provides machine-readable operating-domain taxonomies with restrictive and permissive definitions in formats such as YAML and CSV.
facts.quote: OpenODD (version 1.0.0, 3 April 2025) is a machine-readable way to write an operating-domain taxonomy, with restrictive and permissive definitions, in formats such as YAML and CSV

facts.text: OpenODD's default attributes are on-road, so the manufacturer must write and govern an off-road operating-domain taxonomy.
facts.quote: its default attributes are on-road, so an off-road taxonomy must be written and governed by the manufacturer [Chapter 9].

facts.text: OpenXOntology supplies a shared dictionary giving other formats consistent meanings for terms such as pedestrian and lane; the booklet did not verify OpenXOntology.
facts.quote: OpenXOntology is the shared dictionary that gives the other formats consistent meanings for terms such as "pedestrian" or "lane"; the booklet did not verify it [Chapter 9].

facts.text: ASAM describes the OpenX standards as in maintenance mode in 2026.
facts.quote: ASAM describes the OpenX standards as in maintenance mode (2026)

facts.text: ASAM's OpenX in Off-Road Applications concept project is active, but the booklet considers an off-road extension unlikely before mid-2027.
facts.quote: an "OpenX in Off-Road Applications" concept project is active, but no off-road extension is likely before mid-2027

facts.text: ASAM's off-road workshop identified missing OpenX concepts for deformable and particle terrain, vegetation, heavy-machine manipulation and sensor degradation.
facts.quote: ASAM's own off-road workshop named missing concepts for deformable and particle terrain, vegetation, heavy-machine manipulation and sensor degradation [Chapter 9].

facts.text: Compatibility with scene description formats proves that data can be exchanged, not that simulation physics is correct.
facts.quote: Compatibility with these formats proves that data can be exchanged, not that the physics is right [Chapter 11].

facts.text: The booklet recommends a manufacturer-owned, domain-neutral, version-controlled scenario catalog, using options such as the open-source language Scenic or an in-house YAML schema with an OpenODD-style taxonomy.
facts.quote: encoding the scenario catalog in a domain-neutral, version-controlled form owned by the manufacturer (for example the open-source language Scenic, or an in-house YAML schema with an OpenODD-style taxonomy)

facts.text: The booklet recommends using OpenDRIVE only for structured haul roads, OpenUSD and OpenMATERIAL for scenes, and exporting to OpenSCENARIO where tools require it.
facts.quote: using OpenDRIVE only for structured haul roads, OpenUSD and OpenMATERIAL for scenes, and exporting to OpenSCENARIO where tools need it [Chapter 9].

facts.text: The booklet recommends requiring open-format export as a defense against vendor lock-in and supplier consolidation.
facts.quote: Requiring open-format export is also one of its defenses against vendor lock-in and supplier consolidation [Chapter 11].
